Definition: middle voice of a primary verb; to ward off (for oneself), i.e. protect:--defend.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in Stephen's speech: Moses saw one of his brethren suffer wrong, and he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian. It is the act of stepping in for someone who cannot defend himself — the moment Moses chose his own people over Pharaoh's house.
TheologicalSignificance: One act of defence in one verse carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Moses' choice — he saw the wrong and stepped in, and that choice set the whole course of his life.
